sections.heading: Wire contract
sections.body: A frame starts with a single unsigned length byte and a payload. A fixed-size ring reserves one unused slot so read and write offsets can coincide only when empty.

sections.heading: Independent exercise A
sections.body: Port the enqueue and dequeue functions into the supplied Rust module using safe indexed slices. A short read must preserve both offsets. Reject a frame larger than the usable ring capacity.

sections.heading: Fixtures
sections.body: For a ring of eight slots with an empty state at offset six, enqueue payload bytes 65, 0 and 66, then read the frame. Add tests for this wrap and for retry after an incomplete write.

sections.heading: Independent exercise B
sections.body: Use a saved differential trace to explain how a failed enqueue changes offsets in the old implementation. B requires a short written note only.

holdouts.title: Implement the migration feedback tool
holdouts.description: Add a bounded tool that returns the first divergence in the C and Rust execution traces. Wire it into the repair loop and test it on the three supplied failures.
holdouts.details: Need working code and tests. Analysis plots can wait.

pdf.title: A bounded trace tool for source migration

sections.heading: Given
sections.body: The starter includes parsers in two languages and an instrumented driver. Each operation emits a record with opcode, result, and cursor position. A repair assistant currently receives the entire trace after every attempt. The packet log uses the same monotonically increasing operation index on both sides. Some opcodes produce an empty result field; their cursor positions are still meaningful. A malformed packet must report failure at the first unread byte. Comparing only the final buffer length can hide a faulty repair.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Expose a first_difference operation returning the mismatched record and at most two predecessors. If one side ends early, represent the missing record explicitly. Never include later trace records in the tool response.

sections.heading: Example inputs and output boundary
sections.body: Consider this source trace: (0, open, ok, 0), (1, header, ok, 2), (2, read, short, 2). The translated trace agrees through operation 1 but reports (2, read, short, 3). Your tool must identify index 2 without treating equal return codes as a match. On a trace with no difference, return an explicit no-divergence result; do not fabricate an index. If both traces are empty, that same result must be valid.

sections.heading: Validate
sections.body: Use cases for different return codes, a cursor discrepancy with equal return codes, and one truncated trace. Capture the response on each fixture and verify the repair loop can request it twice without losing the original trace.

sections.heading: Short comparison protocol
sections.body: Run the provided scripted repair sequence with the old whole-trace response, then run it with the bounded response on the same fixtures. In a compact table, record which operation was first flagged and how many records were returned. Explain one case where omitting the preceding records obscures a bad cursor advance. You may use synthetic traces; the parser implementation is outside the repair scope.

sections.heading: Other deliverable
sections.body: A separate report-only track compares saved repair transcripts. It does not require modifying the assistant or rerunning translation.

holdouts.check: Working code plus harness tests should match implementation and debugging, not reviews of the same traces.
